clue.text: One's better to stop using this box

definitions.text: One's better to stop using this box

parts.words: One's better to stop using this box
parts.note: a household cabinet of pills and remedies, which you can stop dipping into once you have recovered from illness

explanation.surface: A puzzling remark that some container can be abandoned once someone has improved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's better' reads as a comparison, but it means 'one has recovered': once well, you no longer need the cabinet of remedies.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue describes the bathroom cupboard holding remedies, used only while unwell.

clue.text: Mechanic initially is thrown, having the wrong part

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word Mechanic

parts.note: to cast is to throw, so thrown gives cast

explanation.surface: A mechanic flings something and finds it is the wrong spare part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part' reads as a spare part, but it is an actor's role: someone miscast plays a part unsuited to them.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor miscast has been given a role that does not suit them, the wrong part.

clue.text: Ultimately bad pub, Irish, with little time for service

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word bad

parts.note: an inn is a pub
Erse is the Gaelic language of Ireland, used for Irish
T is the short abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Complaints about a poor Irish bar where the service is hurried.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' looks like the staff's attention in the pub; it is a matching set of crockery, as in a dinner service.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinner service is a full matching set of plates and dishes for a meal.

clue.text: Pointed feature found on a type of pottery

parts.note: the chin is a facial feature that can be pointed

explanation.surface: A sharp detail turns up on a particular kind of ceramic ware.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pointed feature' sounds like a spout or handle on a pot, but it is a feature of the face.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine porcelain ware is called by this name, after the country it first came from.

clue.text: A weapon upset right-winger, to little effect

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the words A and weapon are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a gun is a weapon
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party, on the political right

explanation.surface: A conservative politician turns a gun over, but nothing much comes of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to little effect' is an adverbial phrase standing for an adjective meaning futile; 'upset' works in a down clue by turning the opening pair of pieces upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nugatory is futile or worthless, achieving little or nothing.

clue.text: Tidies up first of college lists

indicators.note: first of picks out the opening letter of the word college

parts.note: a ship that lists leans to one side

explanation.surface: A college bursar keeps neat inventories, sorting the first of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lists' looks like a noun for inventories but is a verb: to list is to lean over.
explanation.definitionFit: To clean a room is to tidy it up, the same verb in the third person.

clue.text: Great feeling about British plant

indicators.note: about means placed around, so the feeling surrounds the abbreviation

parts.note: euphoria is an intense feeling of joy

explanation.surface: Someone is elated about a home-grown shrub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts B inside EUPHORIA.
explanation.definitionFit: The spurges, a large genus of flowering shrubs and succulents, carry this botanical name.

clue.text: Sailor is turning over bones

parts.note: a tar is an old name for a sailor

indicators.note: turning over means the word is is flipped so its letters run backwards

explanation.surface: A seaman is rolling over some bones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning over' affects only the word just before it, not the sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the small bones of the ankle, or of an insect's foot, in plural form.

clue.text: Support mostly weak in chaotic state

parts.note: a bed is a supporting base, as a bed of concrete

indicators.note: mostly means almost all of a word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: lame means feeble or weak, as a lame excuse

explanation.surface: A rickety support lies in a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts the E from LAME to give LAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedlam, named after an old London asylum, means uproar and confusion.

clue.text: Vice boss is failing

parts.note: a vice is a sin
a king is the head or boss

explanation.surface: A crime lord's empire is collapsing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vice boss' reads as a gangland chief, but it splits into two pieces: a moral failing and a ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: Going under or declining, as a sinking business is a failing one.

clue.text: Assisting side of Briton abroad, bagging runs with energy

indicators.note: bagging means capturing, so the expatriate holds the runs inside

parts.note: an expat is someone living abroad, such as a Briton overseas
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An Englishman overseas scores runs energetically for his team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bagging' puts R inside EXPAT. The Latin legal term means on behalf of one side only, so it describes helping one party.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin legal phrase means made on behalf of, or in the interest of, one party only.

clue.text: A historical period recalled in Wembley, say

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the phrase is read in reverse

parts.note: the article a becomes an before a vowel sound, as in an era
an era is a historical period

explanation.surface: A bygone age is remembered at the famous stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wembley, say' is a definition by example: the stadium is one instance of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Wembley, London's national football stadium, is one example of a venue for sport, signalled by 'say'.

clue.text: Barber's soon upset in court case

indicators.note: in puts the shuffled letters inside the legal case

parts.note: a trial is a case heard in court

indicators.note: upset means knocked into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A hairdresser is soon distressed by a lawsuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barber's' looks like a possessive noun but stands for an adjective meaning 'of barbers'.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means relating to hairdressing, so it does the work of the possessive 'barber's'.

clue.text: Cricket scoring system shown on TV in an idle moment?

definitions.text: shown on TV in an idle moment?

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket match
a card records the score, as in a scorecard

explanation.surface: Cricket's scoreboard flashes up on television during a lull.
explanation.walkthrough: The test card was the still image British TV broadcast when no programmes were on air.
explanation.definitionFit: A test card was a static image screened when the channel had nothing scheduled, during idle hours.

clue.text: Note in note-case rewritten in an Eastern language

indicators.note: rewritten means set down again in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A banknote placed in a wallet is translated into an Asian tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rewritten' shuffles N and NOTECASE together.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Chinese variety spoken in Guangdong and Hong Kong, a language of the East.

clue.text: Flourishing line, in a successful period

indicators.note: in means the letter is placed within the following phrase

parts.note: a boom is a time of prosperity

explanation.surface: A business line thrives in the good times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts L inside A BOOM.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant in full flower is in bloom, so the adjective means thriving or flourishing.

clue.text: Love? Poet's bad, upset, a shade unsparkling, maybe

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the words upside down, so the phrase runs from the bottom

parts.note: a bard is a poet
evil means bad

explanation.surface: A lovelorn poet writes badly and is distressed by his dull work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' acts on the poet and the badness together, not on the love; the definition joins a colour name with a word for dull.
explanation.definitionFit: This greyish-green khaki colour is a shade that is notably dull, without any sparkle.

clue.text: Basic skill with sword should include skill for riposte

parts.note: the three Rs are the basic skills of reading, writing and arithmetic, so R is one

indicators.note: include means take inside, so the sword holds the next word

parts.note: an epee is a fencing sword
art is skill, as in the art of fencing

explanation.surface: A fencer's grounding with the blade should take in the craft of the counter-thrust.
explanation.walkthrough: The three Rs (reading, writing, arithmetic) are the basic school skills, so 'Basic skill' can give one R.
explanation.definitionFit: Repartee is quick witty retort, a verbal riposte borrowed from fencing.

clue.text: One shuns ill person, getting clear

indicators.note: shuns means avoids, so the numeral is left out

parts.note: a patient is someone under medical care
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A sick person avoids company and recovers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shuns' removes I from PATIENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Patent can mean obvious or evident, as in a patent lie.

clue.text: A difficult situation, to choose most of cricket side

parts.note: to pick is to choose

indicators.note: most of means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: the leg side is one half of a cricket field, the batter's side

explanation.surface: A selector is in a jam choosing most of the cricket team.
explanation.walkthrough: LEG side is the half of a cricket field behind the batter's legs; 'most of' cuts it to LE.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a pickle is to be in a predicament or tricky fix.

clue.text: Went to court about republic getting back historic coin

indicators.note: getting back means returning, so the whole is read backwards
about means surrounding, so the legal action wraps the country

parts.note: to sue is to go to law, so sued means went to court
Iran is an Islamic republic

explanation.surface: A state that was sued is recovering an ancient coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting back' works on the whole assembled container, not just the country.
explanation.definitionFit: The denarius was a silver coin of ancient Rome.

clue.text: Industry whose activity goes on in all circumstances?

definitions.text: Industry whose activity goes on in all circumstances?

parts.words: Industry whose activity goes on in all circumstances?
parts.note: an allusion to the saying that the show must go on, applied to the entertainment trade

explanation.surface: A business that never stops working regardless of conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue alludes to the motto of entertainers, 'the show must go on'.
explanation.definitionFit: The entertainment industry is informally called by this name, and its motto is that performance continues regardless.

clue.text: Still a problem on the radio?

definitions.meaning: crackling interference heard on a radio broadcast

explanation.surface: Radio interference persists.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both motionless and the crackling interference on radio reception.

clue.text: Groups of companies, the type one's seen in study article

indicators.note: seen in means placed inside, so the next pieces go within the other two

parts.note: to con is to study or learn
a is the indefinite article
a sort is a type or kind
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Business groupings are examined in a study piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the' before 'type' is padding; CON for study is an old crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: A consortium is an association of firms; the Latin plural names several of them.

clue.text: French city, half new, being built up

indicators.note: in a down clue built up means the words are stacked from the bottom, so they read upwards

parts.note: semi is a prefix meaning half

explanation.surface: A town in France is half new as it is being developed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being built up' turns SEMI N round to give the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Nîmes is a city in southern France, known for its Roman arena.

clue.text: Belief company's in red? On the contrary

indicators.note: in, with the reversal that follows, means one piece is placed within the other
on the contrary says the clue's arrangement is swapped, so red goes inside company rather than the reverse

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether the firm's creed is socialist.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue says the company is in red, but 'On the contrary' swaps container and contents.
explanation.definitionFit: A credo is a set of beliefs or a creed, from the Latin for 'I believe'.

clue.text: Just a bit, from a certain vineyard, supported by doctor

indicators.note: in a down clue supported by means the next piece sits below

parts.note: a cru is a French vineyard or its classified growth
MB is a medical degree, Bachelor of Medicine

explanation.surface: Only a drop of wine from a chosen estate is allowed by the doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'supported by' puts the doctor underneath; Bachelor of Medicine is a doctor's degree.
explanation.definitionFit: A crumb is a tiny fragment, so it means only a little of something.

clue.text: Shining example of complaint about book

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the grievance wraps the letter

parts.note: a lament is a cry of grief or complaint

explanation.surface: An outstanding grievance concerns a volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shining example' reads as one idiom; split it after 'Shining' and 'example of' just joins definition to wordplay. 'about' puts B inside LAMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambent means glowing softly or flickering, as a lambent flame.

clue.text: Bone brute cracked, hugging Rita, half broken off

indicators.note: hugging means holding inside, so the shuffled word wraps the next piece
cracked means broken apart, so the letters of brute are rearranged
half broken off leaves only the first half of the name

explanation.surface: A thug cracks a rib while squeezing Rita.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hugging' puts the short half-name inside the shuffled thug, splitting it after its fourth letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A true rib is one of the upper ribs joined directly to the breastbone.

clue.text: Dope's pictures not completed for Dickens book

indicators.note: not completed means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: drawings by a fool, a bozo being a dope, give sketches by bozo

explanation.surface: An idiot's unfinished drawings are offered as a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: BOZO is slang for a fool; 'not completed' cuts its last O. Boz was Dickens's early pen name.
explanation.definitionFit: This was Dickens's first book, a collection of sketches published under his pen name Boz.
